dimensions.assessment: Affects pregnant women enrolled in Medicaid and CHIP, state health agencies, and medical test providers.
dimensions.evidence: pregnant women with preeclampsia who are eligible for and receiving medical assistance under a State plan... or a State child health plan

dimensions.assessment: Requires federal issuance of best practices guidance and technical assistance to clarify coverage options, leaving direct coverage decisions largely to states.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretary shall issue guidance to States... on best practices for improving outcomes... and which tests... may be covered

dimensions.assessment: Involves administrative costs for issuing guidance and providing technical assistance, but does not mandate direct federal spending increases or specific appropriations.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretary shall issue guidance to States... and provide such technical assistance to such State

dimensions.assessment: Amends Title XIX of the Social Security Act to add a section requiring specific federal guidance and technical assistance on preeclampsia tests.
dimensions.evidence: Title XIX of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396 et seq.) is amended by inserting after section 1948 the following new section

dimensions.assessment: Imposes a one-time deadline of 180 days for issuing guidance, with ongoing technical assistance available upon state request.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than the date that is 180 days after the date of the enactment of this section, the Secretary shall issue guidance

Specific cost of administering the technical assistance program
importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires the HHS Secretary to issue guidance and technical assistance to States regarding Medicaid and CHIP coverage of preeclampsia screening and early detection tests.
